To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) disentangled representations in deep neural networks can be achieved by training with the help of a disentangled latent space prior, which can be learned from the data; (2) the disentangled representations can be used for a variety of downstream tasks such as semi-supervised classification, domain adaptation, and out-of-distribution detection.

(1) the activations in deep networks are disentangled in a sense similar to that of the VAE, but (2) they are disentangled with respect to the input data, not the latent representation, and (3) this disentanglement is a consequence of the network’s architecture, and not a result of any particular training procedure.

(a) deep learning is a good approach for learning the representations of images, (b) deep learning is not a good approach for understanding what the representations of images mean, and (c) deep learning is an excellent approach for understanding what a deep neural network is doing.
